queries.arg:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.network/applicationgateways'
| project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, sku
| join kind=leftouter (
    Resources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/applicationgateways'
    | mv-expand pool = properties.backendAddressPools limit 2000
    | extend ipCount = array_length(pool.properties.backendIPConfigurations),
        addressCount = array_length(pool.properties.backendAddresses)
    | summarize backendTargets = sum(coalesce(ipCount, 0) + coalesce(addressCount, 0)) by id
) on id
| where coalesce(backendTargets, 0) == 0
| project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, sku, backendTargets

queryEvidence.assessment: Retain exactly. Leftouter includes empty pool arrays; sum tests visible targets across backend IP configurations and backend addresses. Missing properties, visibility, eventual consistency and expansion/paging limits can affect interpretation. This does not assess traffic/utilization or authorize deletion.

queries.arg:

| where type =~ 'microsoft.network/expressroutecircuits'

    peeringLocation = tostring(properties.serviceProviderProperties.peeringLocation),
    bandwidthMbps = tolong(properties.serviceProviderProperties.bandwidthInMbps)

before.name: wafsg-AzureResourceManagerLockMaliciousDeletion
before.title: Use an appropriate resource lock to protect the storage account's control plane.
before.description: A CanNotDelete lock helps prevent deletion of the storage account through Azure Resource Manager while allowing normal configuration changes. ReadOnly is more restrictive and can interfere with operations such as key listing and role assignment. Neither lock prevents data-plane deletion or modification of blobs, files, queues or tables. Combine locks with least-privilege access, service-level protection and recovery controls, and restrict who can remove a lock.

before.title: Before initiating a failover or failback, evaluate the potential for data loss by checking the value of the last synchronization time property. This recommendation applies only to GRS and GZRS configurations.
before.description: This property helps you estimate how much data you might lose by initiating an account failover. All data and metadata written before the last synchronization time is available on the secondary region, but data and metadata written after the last synchronization time might be lost because it's not written to the secondary region.

afterChanges.description:
This property helps you estimate how much data you might lose by initiating an account failover. All data and metadata written before the last synchronization time is available on the secondary region, but data and metadata written after the last synchronization time might be lost because it's not written to the secondary region.

This property helps you estimate how much data you might lose if you initiate an account failover. All data and metadata that's written before the last synchronization time is available on the secondary region, but you might lose data and metadata that's written after the last synchronization time because it's not written to the secondary region.

Interpret these statements as potential loss: writes after Last Sync Time might already have replicated, but are not guaranteed. Assess customer-managed unplanned failover separately from planned failover and failback, for which data loss is not expected while both regions remain available throughout the operation. GRS and GZRS here include their read-access variants; this guidance does not apply to LRS or ZRS alone.
